subject.title: Session lane starvation: followup drain monopolizes session lane, blocks inbound dispatch for 20-30min

question: Should OpenClaw make foreground user/channel messages preempt, interrupt, or yield queued background/follow-up work for the same session by default?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the fix determines product semantics for queue modes, STOP/abort behavior, transcript ordering, and background task reliability; automation should not choose that contract unaided.

options.title: User messages win by default
options.body: Make visible inbound user/control work interrupt, preempt, or force-yield background and follow-up drains while keeping background work best-effort.

options.title: Bound consecutive follow-ups
options.body: Keep existing follow-up semantics but cap consecutive drain turns or elapsed drain time and re-check foreground admission between queued turns.

options.title: Keep current queue contract
options.body: Document the current followup/collect waiting behavior and rely on operational mitigations rather than changing scheduler precedence.

recommendation.title: User messages win by default
recommendation.body: Make visible inbound user/control work interrupt, preempt, or force-yield background and follow-up drains while keeping background work best-effort.
